headline: Chips Lead a Broad Friday Rally as Traders Brace for a Geopolitically Charged October
body_html:
Friday's session closed the week on a constructive note, with 365 stocks advancing against 174 declining across the 544-name universe. Semiconductors were the undisputed engine of the day, surging 4.18% as a group and pulling the broader tape higher. MaxLinear jumped nearly 15% and Synaptics added 14.08%, while Allegro MicroSystems rose 8.66%, making the chip complex the clearest source of conviction on the day. Industrials and Materials also posted solid gains of 1.33% and 1.16%, respectively, with freight operator RXO Inc climbing 9.46% and advanced-materials specialist Materion adding 9.48%.

Not every corner of the market shared in the optimism. Storage names took a sharp hit, with Western Digital and Seagate Technology each tumbling more than 10%. Homebuilders slipped 0.73% and Software edged fractionally lower, suggesting pockets of rate or demand sensitivity remain a headwind even on up days.

Heading into Monday, October 5, traders face a geopolitical backdrop that grew noisier over the weekend — tensions in the Middle East, reports of Saudi-led planning against Houthi forces, and elevated oil-market focus following the IEA's commentary on falling crude prices. Energy stocks gained 0.84% Friday; how that sector responds to weekend headlines will be worth watching at the open.

briefs.headline: Storage Stocks Suffer Their Worst Day in Months
briefs.body: Western Digital and Seagate Technology each shed roughly 10% on Friday, making storage the session's most conspicuous casualty. The simultaneous sell-off in both names pointed to a sector-wide concern rather than company-specific news, and traders will be watching for any clarifying catalysts when markets reopen Monday.

briefs.headline: IEA Chief Flags Declining Oil Prices After Reserve Decision
briefs.body: International Energy Agency head Fatih Birol indicated that crude prices have begun to soften following a coordinated reserve-release decision. The development landed as Energy stocks closed Friday up 0.84%, a gain that may face a fresh test Monday as markets weigh the agency's outlook against escalating Red Sea supply-route uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Saudi Arabia Weighs Military Move Against Houthis to Reopen Red Sea Lanes
briefs.body: Reports over the weekend described Saudi Arabia planning an offensive against Houthi forces in a bid to end the prolonged disruption to Red Sea shipping. The corridor is a critical artery for global freight, and any escalation or resolution could have immediate ripple effects on freight and energy stocks when trading resumes.

briefs.headline: Skilled-Trade Labour Gap Looms Over Industrial Sector Outlook
briefs.body: A new report projects 1.7 million skilled-trade job openings per year through 2035, with experts uncertain where the workforce will come from. For the Industrials sector — which gained 1.33% on Friday — a structural labour shortage of that scale could constrain capacity and weigh on margins over the medium term.

briefs.headline: UK Auto Market Posts Strong September, EVs and Chinese Brands Gain Share
briefs.body: British new-car registrations climbed 12% in September, led in part by electric vehicles and emerging Chinese marques. The data adds to a growing body of evidence that EV adoption in Europe is accelerating, with competitive pressure from Chinese manufacturers reshaping the traditional automotive landscape.

briefs.headline: Private Capital Deepens Its Footprint in Hollywood Production
briefs.body: Institutional and private capital is playing an increasingly prominent role in financing film and television projects, shifting influence away from legacy studio balance sheets. The trend has broad implications for media valuations and content economics, and may attract closer attention from Consumer-sector analysts as deal flow continues to build.
